catalyst: Question 8 would end adult-use retail sales (medical kept) — first-ever repeal vote on a legal market
ib_angle: Binary event for ~800 licensed businesses; polls show repeal trailing badly (Suffolk/Boston Globe, Oct 20: 71% no / 21% yes; UMass Amherst: 55% no / 33% yes). Defeat lifts an overhang on MA valuations.

catalyst: Adult-use left out of the FY26-27 budget (signed Jul 12); every House seat and half the Senate are on the Nov 3 ballot; next vehicle is the FY27-28 budget
ib_angle: Medical-only with capped permits keeps doors scarce (Cresco paid $50M for 9 stores). Adult-use passage would re-rate incumbents.

catalyst: Adult-use retail sales start Jul 1, 2027; Cannabis Control Authority opens license applications Feb 1, 2027; 350-store cap; 6% state tax (8% after Jul 2029)
ib_angle: Greenfield build-out: applicants need capital and operating partners; existing vertical medical operators are best placed to convert.

catalyst: DOH final order (Sep 11) issued all 22 new vertically integrated MMTC licenses from the 2023 round; losing applicants had 30 days to appeal and appeals were expected; adult-use ballot dismissed — next attempt 2028
ib_angle: Each new licensee must post $5M of financial assurance within 10 business days and fund a build-out → financing, JV and sale mandates; incumbents are consolidating (Vireo–FLUENT, Planet 13).

catalyst: SB 56 (eff. Mar 20): 400-dispensary statewide cap (~200 open), 8-store per-operator limit, 1-mile spacing between stores, 70% THC cap on extracts
ib_angle: Capped adult-use market with room to grow; distressed exits (Cannabist→Holistic $47M, AYR→Arboretum) and Vireo's 4-deal vertical entry.

catalyst: HB 46 TCUP expansion: 12 new dispensing licenses conditionally awarded (9 in Dec 2025, 3 in Apr 2026; tabulation corrected May 8); licensees must be operational within 24 months
ib_angle: Build-out capital for new licensees; the 2027 session could widen the program further.

catalyst: State Supreme Court upheld the voter-approved medical law (Sep 4); first round of 4 product-manufacturing licenses (applications closed Jul 20) to be awarded by lottery
ib_angle: Greenfield medical market; early license holders become tuck-in targets.

catalyst: Adult-use retail licensing restarted under SB 3313: up to 24 retail licenses across six zones; applications due Nov 23; federal judge dismissed the three licensing suits as moot (Oct 21)
ib_angle: New doors in a small market next to MA and CT operators.

catalyst: $1.1B annual market; TerrAscend paid $9M for a single store doing more than $10M a year
ib_angle: Scarce, high-volume doors in key counties support MSO tuck-ins.

catalyst: 87 retailers (~12% of licensees) on OCM's cash-on-delivery list owing ~$3.89M to 44 suppliers, ~281 days delinquent on average; OCM's largest illicit seizure (>$17M)
ib_angle: Stressed single-store retailers → tuck-ins and distressed sales.

catalyst: First year of statewide adult-use retail (from Sep 16, 2025): >$250M combined sales (~$150M adult-use, ~$100M medical); 369 licensed businesses; 486,720 plants held by 102 license holders
ib_angle: Young adult-use market scaling quickly; supply build-out and licensee capital needs.

catalyst: Most active 2026 M&A state: Vireo (Schwazze, LivWell, Cannabist stores) and Spherex buying Cannabist grows; declining cultivation capacity
ib_angle: Mature, price-compressed market where scale buyers are consolidating at low per-door prices.

catalyst: Regulators approved Vireo–Planet 13 on Oct 15; Vireo closed C21 (Aug 21) and M3 Wellness (Sep 21)
ib_angle: Consolidation of tourist-driven retail; remaining independents are natural targets.

catalyst: Governor's advisory council issues regulatory recommendations in Dec 2026 as a 2027 roadmap; 63% back adult-use, 74% medical (SurveyUSA)
ib_angle: Large state with no regulated program; position ahead of 2027 bills.

catalyst: Only Democratic-trifecta state without adult-use; Gov. Green has said he would sign a bill
ib_angle: Legislative path is the clearest of the remaining holdouts.

catalyst: Open governor's race and legislative seats on Nov 3 could put legalization on the 2027 agenda
ib_angle: Surrounded by legal markets; outcome sets 2027 odds.

catalyst: Senate killed House-passed legalization in 2026; Gov. Ayotte opposes and vetoed a medical grow expansion
ib_angle: Low near-term odds; last New England holdout.

catalyst: HJR 4 would give the Legislature sole power to legalize, ending citizen initiatives; medical initiative failed to qualify
ib_angle: Would close the initiative path in a no-program state.

catalyst: 24% wholesale excise since Jan 1, 2026 on top of the 10% retail excise and 6% sales tax
ib_angle: Margin compression is producing distressed sellers.

catalyst: Patient registry passed 55,000 (56,650 as of Sep 23), raising each producer's dispensary cap from 5 to 9; dispensary application window for the six existing producers Oct 26–30; new medical delivery rule (Sep 30) allows USPS shipment
ib_angle: Higher per-producer store cap creates build-out capital needs in a tightly licensed medical market; delivery adds distribution reach.

catalyst: Market topped $2B a year by 2024 and is now in a correction
ib_angle: Price compression pressures smaller operators; limited-license structure still supports values.

catalyst: Local opt-outs still the rule nine years after legalization; Vireo–Eaze adds delivery scale
ib_angle: Fragmented, oversupplied market; delivery and distribution are the consolidation plays.
